newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates, govt paper mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates, govt paper mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Hong Kong Interbank rates and government paper were mixed on Tuesday in quiet trading with the market lacking direction because the U.S. markets were closed for a holiday on Monday, dealers said.

"Trading is quiet as the U.S. market was closed and there is important data to be released tomorrow," a Japanese bank dealer said. The U.S. will announce its September Consumer Prices Index (CPI) on Wednesday, he added.
Overnight money was slightly up at 5-1/16 five percent against 5-1/16 4-15/16, while three-month money eased to 5-1/2 3/8 from 5-9/16 7/16 percent.
Trading in government paper was quiet with dealers noting firm support in the newly-launched three-year notes.
"Investors are likely to be a bit short on the three-year notes and that will give the issue some support," an European bank dealer said.
One-week Exchange Fund bills yielded 4.82 percent versus 4.83 percent and three-year notes yielded 6.46 versus 6.44.
The yield on five-year notes was 7.01 versus 7.02 and on seven-year notes, 7.36 from 7.37.
